summary: Clallam County lookout site with a 1917 station and a 1918 salary note; sources disagree whether it is the Kloshe Nanitch lookout; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone; firelookout.com marks it abandoned. No source describes a structure at the Muller location.
facts.agency: Washington Division of Forestry/DNR (the Washington Lookouts index says State Department of Forestry)

events.note: A 1917 Tacoma Times headline, as quoted by WillhiteWeb, announces that the state is installing a fire lookout station on Muller Mountain. No source describes a structure.
The Washington Forest Fire Association paid part of the salary of the lookout stationed on 'Mt. Mueller' (11th Annual Report, as quoted by WillhiteWeb and the Washington Lookouts index).
Only if Muller is the Kloshe Nanitch site: WillhiteWeb says the USFS had the reconstructed D-6 cupola removed as a public nuisance and left the platform in place.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WillhiteWeb argues the Muller, Solduc and Burnt Mountain names all refer to Kloshe Nanitch. The FFLOS list gives Muller its own coordinates, firelookout.com gives it 3,748 feet three miles WNW of Lake Crescent, and the Washington Lookouts index gives Muller 30N-10W-15 against 30N-11W-23 for Kloshe Nanitch. The story keeps the question open and does not merge the two records.

notes_for_editor: Probably the same site as us-wa-kloshe-nanitch, or a near neighbour; editor should decide whether to merge or keep separate. WillhiteWeb's identity argument is an opinion, not a survey; the page itself says its author would be glad to be proven wrong. Elevations disagree: firelookout.com gives Muller 3,748 ft, WillhiteWeb gives Kloshe Nanitch 3,160 ft. The 1917 date rests on a newspaper headline quoted second-hand, so the event is typed 'other' (announced installation), not 'built'. The 2013 removal event is conditional on the identity question. No abandonment year, no structure description, no access facts. The same WillhiteWeb page also says the Kloshe Nanich lookout 'was destroyed in 1963', which conflicts with its later cupola reconstruction and 2013 removal; the story does not use the 1963 claim.
